# Student Volunteer Service “Time Bank” Design

## 1. Project Overview

"Time Bank" is a volunteer service management model for middle school students. The system converts the service hours generated by students' participation in volunteer services into "time coins" that can be recorded, accumulated, queried, and audited according to unified rules, forming students' personal "time wealth."

This document is the **top-level solution design** of Time Bank, focusing on system goals, core concepts, service requirements, core functions, role division and incentive system, and does not include specific implementation details of auditing, data, online and offline, and blockchain. The relevant implementation is split into the following independent sub-solutions:

- **`02-ManualAudit.md`**: Current stage of manual audit plan and service record data design.
- **`03-AutoAudit.md`**: Automatic audit scheme (POV witness audit), witness metadata and implementation path analysis.
- **`04-Blockchain.md`**: Blockchain certification scheme, compliance requirements, public chain selection and cost assessment.
- **`05-OnlineSystem.md`**: Online system design and simple implementation plan.
- **`06-Legal.md`**: Legal constraints of blockchain applications under Chinese laws and regulations, legal restrictions and legalization paths of time coin.
- **`07-AI.md`**: AI technology application solution, covering client-side face desensitization, multi-modal content review, image authenticity detection, statistical anomaly risk control and witness credit scoring.

## 2. Project background and construction significance

### 2.1 Background

The school has currently established student volunteer service requirements and records student service information through a paper version of the "Student Volunteer Service Record Form". The existing method can meet the basic registration and audit needs, but there are the following problems in long-term management:

- **Records are scattered**: Student personal service records mainly rely on paper forms, and filing, query and statistical efficiency are low.
- **Long review link**: After the service is completed, manual submission, manual verification, and manual summary are required, which is prone to omissions or delays.
- **Insufficient incentive mechanism**: Service length is currently mainly used for graduation or further education requirements, and there is a lack of continuous value feedback.
- **Insufficient data accumulation**: It is difficult for schools to analyze student growth, optimize public welfare projects, and coordinate resources based on volunteer service data.

### 2.2 Construction significance

Time Bank further establishes a long-term incentive mechanism for students' public welfare participation on the basis of meeting the service length requirements for graduation by converting volunteer service hours into "time coins".

- **For students**: Clarify service goals, accumulate personal public welfare results, and obtain a sense of accomplishment and growth records.
- **For schools**: Improve the efficiency of volunteer service management and form a data system that can be counted, tracked, and evaluated.
- **For communities and public welfare organizations**: Establish a stable supply of student volunteer services and promote the linkage of schools and social welfare resources.
- **For Student Development Center**: Form a unified service identification, review, recording and feedback mechanism.

## 3. Project goals

### 3.1 Overall Goal

Build a set of student volunteer service time banking mechanisms suitable for middle schools to achieve standardized management, digital precipitation and incentive operations of volunteer services.

### 3.2 Stage Goals

| Stages | Objectives | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 1: Offline operation | Establish unified rules and paper recording process | Use existing volunteer service schedule for manual recording, regular review and cumulative statistics |
| Second stage: Complete Web system | Build a time bank platform that can operate independently | Merge the original "semi-digital management" and "online system management" to provide student entrance and administrator/teacher entrance, covering projects, registration, service records, manual review, accounts, statistics, import and export and system management, ensuring that the whole process can be completed without relying on WeChat or other IM |
| The third stage: WeChat applet and POV | Increase mobile on-site witnessing capabilities | Build a WeChat applet on a complete Web system, focusing on POV processes such as on-site shooting, location check-in, witness QR code scanning, terminal-side desensitization, team member mutual certification and guardian endorsement |
| The fourth stage: value expansion | Enable and operate exchange, lending, and value-added mechanisms | In the second stage, the Web system reserves or completes corresponding management capabilities. In this stage, after the rules and cooperation resources are clear, goods, services, honors, compensation, and value-added scenarios will be opened cautiously |

## 4. Core concept definition

### 4.1 Volunteer Service Time

The effective service hours generated by the students’ actual completion of voluntary services in projects recognized by the school on campus, off campus, community, public welfare organizations or student development centers.

### 4.2 Time Coin

Time coins are the recording unit of volunteer service time. The basic conversion rules are:

> 1 hour of volunteering = 1 time coin

Time coins are not equivalent to real currency, do not have cash properties, cannot be bought and sold privately, cannot be transferred, and cannot be used for commercial transactions. Its use is limited to volunteer service management, motivation, redemption, compensation and growth recording scenarios approved by the school.

### 4.3 Time wealth

The personal volunteer service results accumulated by students in the time bank include accumulated service hours, accumulated time coins, service categories, service projects, audit records, honor records and exchange records.

### 4.4 Effective Services

Valid services must meet the following conditions at the same time:

- **Project source compliance**: It belongs to the volunteer service channel recognized by the school.
- **Real service content**: Students actually participate in and complete service tasks.
- **Complete record information**: including service date, length, location, organization, supervisor's signature or certification materials.
- **Approved**: Reviewed and confirmed by the Student Development Center or the teacher in charge of the grade.

## 5. Applicable objects and management scope

### 5.1 Applicable objects

This program is suitable for middle school students and focuses on:

- Junior high school students in grades six to eight
- High school students in grades 9 to 11
- Teachers and student leaders involved in organizing, recording, reviewing, and managing volunteer service


### 5.2 Management Scope

Time bank covers the following volunteer service management matters:

- Release and claim of volunteer service projects
- Student registration and task assignment
- Service process records
- Review of service hours
- Time coin conversion and storage
- Graduation service requirement statistics
- Lending, exchange, compensation and incentive mechanisms
- Data analysis and growth file precipitation

## 6. Volunteer service time requirements

### 6.1 Requirements for junior middle school students

| Grade | Annual Requirements | Stage Cumulative Requirements | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sixth grade | Minimum of 25 hours per year | 75 hours cumulative by graduation | Cumulative starting in sixth grade |
| Seventh grade | Minimum of 25 hours per year | 50 cumulative hours for graduation | Students inserted into or counted from seventh grade must meet cumulative requirement |
| Eighth Grade | Meets Advancement Requirements | 25 hours Total | Requires Completion of Minimum Pre-Admission Service Requirements |

At the junior high school level, it is recommended that a total of 75 hours in three years be used as the complete goal, and individual case identification is allowed based on the student's entrance grade, transfer status, and school policies for the year.

### 6.2 Requirements for high school level

| Grade | Annual Requirements | Stage Cumulative Requirements | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ninth grade | At least 75 hours per year | 300 cumulative hours by graduation | Starting point for cumulative volunteer service in high school |
| 10th grade | Minimum 75 hours per year | 300 cumulative hours by graduation | Continuing cumulative hours of service |
| Eleventh grade | Meets graduation requirements | 75 hours total | Gap due to be completed prior to graduation review |

At the high school level, a total of 300 hours in three years is required for graduation qualifications. For transfer students, students with special projects, or students who fail to complete the year due to objective reasons, a supplementary review mechanism should be established by the Student Development Center.

## 7. Access to volunteer services

### 7.1 On-campus volunteering

On-campus volunteer service is an important channel for students to participate in school public affairs and campus activities, including:

- **Campus Activity Organization**: Plan, prepare, and execute various campus activities.
- **Event site management**: Maintain event order, assist with security and on-site guidance.
- **Academic event support**: Support lectures, seminars, open days, exhibitions, and similar activities.
- **Student Independent Project**: Innovative volunteer services independently initiated by students and recognized by the Student Development Center.
- **Other recognition work**: The Student Development Center reviews the recognized service tasks based on the actual situation.

### 7.2 Off-campus volunteer services

Off-campus volunteer services need to emphasize authenticity, public welfare and safety, including:

- **Community volunteer services**: community construction, environmental beautification, resident assistance, public services, etc.
- **Public welfare organization cooperation projects**: Services carried out in cooperation with off-campus public welfare institutions and non-profit organizations.
- **Government or public agency projects**: Public service voluntary projects approved by the school.
- **Special social welfare activities**: such as public welfare publicity, environmental protection activities, helping the elderly and the disabled, educational support, etc.

### 7.3 Project identification principles

Volunteer service projects should comply with the following principles:

- **Public Welfare**: The purpose is to serve others, serve the community, and serve the public interest.
- **Non-profit**: The main purpose shall not be commercial sales, personal profit or disguised labor substitution.
- **Security**: The service location, task content and organizer must have basic security guarantees.
- **Provability**: Service processes and duration can be recorded, proven and audited.
- **Educational**: Can promote students' sense of responsibility, cooperation ability, social understanding and self-growth.

## 8. Core function design

### 8.1 Saving Function Saving Function

The savings function is the basic function of time bank and is used to record and save students’ volunteer service hours.

#### Function content

- Record the date, duration, location, organization and task content of each student's service.
- After passing the review, the service time will be converted into time coins.
- Time wealth is accumulated in the student's personal account.
- Supports statistics by student, class, grade, service category and project source.

#### Run rules

- Only valid services that have passed the review can be credited to the account.
- 1 hour of effective service is counted as 1 time coin.
- Services of less than 1 hour can be recorded in units of 0.5 hours, as specified by the school.
- The same service shall not be submitted repeatedly or entered into accounts repeatedly.

### 8.2 Borrowing Function Borrowing Function

The loan function is a function to be developed and is mainly used to solve the problem of individual students temporarily failing to meet the standards at the graduation or further education stage.

#### Applicable scenarios

- Students have insufficient service hours due to objective reasons such as transfer of schools, sick leave, special family circumstances, etc.
- Students are approaching graduation or further education review points, and there is a small gap in service time.
- After evaluation by the Student Development Center, the student has a clear follow-up plan to make up the tuition.

#### Suggested Rules

- The borrowing amount should be capped, e.g. no more than 10% of the total stage requirements.
- Loan needs to be applied by the student himself, confirmed by the class teacher or grade-level teacher, and approved by the Student Development Center.
- Borrowed time coins are only used to temporarily meet graduation or further education review and cannot be used to exchange for goods or services.
- Students must repay the borrowed hours through subsequent volunteer service within the specified period.
- Students who fail to return their materials on time should enter the reminder, interview and remediation process.

### 8.3 Redemption Function

The exchange function is an important way to realize the value of time coin, and it is currently in the negotiation and follow-up development stage.

#### Redeemable content

- **Honorary Category**: Volunteer Service Certificate, Annual Charity Star, and Outstanding Volunteer Title.
- **Growth category**: student growth file records, recommendation letter materials, public welfare project display opportunities.
- **Service Category**: Priority registration for on-campus activities, workshop quotas, mentor exchange opportunities.
- **Physical objects**: low-value non-cash items such as school cultural creations and charity-themed souvenirs.

#### Exchange Principles

- The exchange mechanism should highlight the educational significance and public welfare value and avoid excessive materialization.
- Time coins cannot be exchanged for cash and cannot be used for commercial consumption.
- Redemption should be set up at different levels to guide students to participate in the long term.
- Exchange records should be kept in personal time bank accounts.

### 8.4 Value-added function Appreciation Function

Value-added functions are a later development direction and are used to encourage sustained, high-quality, and long-term investment in volunteer services.

#### Possible mechanism

- **Continuous Service Bonus**: If you steadily participate in similar projects for multiple consecutive semesters, you can receive additional honor points or time coin rewards.
- **High Responsibility Position Bonus**: Serving as a project leader, training new volunteers, and undertaking organizational and coordination tasks can earn additional recognition.
- **Special project bonus**: Special incentives can be set for key public welfare projects of the school and long-term community cooperation projects.

#### Risk Control

Value-added functions should be carefully designed to prevent students from neglecting service quality in pursuit of time coins. All bonus rules must be open, transparent, and auditable.

### 8.5 Compensation Function Compensation Function

The compensation mechanism is used to deal with the determination of service time under special circumstances.

#### Applicable situations

- The student actually completed the service, but failed to sign in time due to the organizer's reasons.
- After the school unified organized activities, there were omissions in the student list or duration statistics.
- Students who miss service opportunities due to force majeure need to arrange alternative projects.

#### Processing method

- Students submit applications for supplementary admission and relevant supporting materials.
- The teacher in charge of the grade will conduct the preliminary review.
- The Student Development Center will review and decide whether to supplement the admission.
- The reasons must be marked for supplementary records to facilitate subsequent traceability.

## 9. Business process design

### 9.1 Overall process

The basic process of time bank is as follows:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
A[Release or identify volunteer service projects] --> B[Students claim work]
B --> C [Complete service task]
C --> D [Fill in volunteer service schedule]
D --> E[Submit for review]
E --> F {whether the review is passed}
F -- Pass --> G [Convert to Time Coin]
G --> H [Deposit into personal account]
H --> I[accumulated time wealth]
F -- Fail --> J [Return for supplement or reject]
```

### 9.2 Process steps (overview)

- **Project release or recognition**: School release, student independent application or off-campus cooperation project, clarify the content, time, place, number of people, person in charge and duration recognition method.
- **Student sign-up**: Students claim tasks based on their interests and availability.
- **Complete Service**: Students complete as required and comply with discipline and safety regulations.
- **Record Service**: Students complete service records.
- **Submit for Review**: Verify authenticity and compliance through manual or automated review.
- **Accounting and Depositing**: After passing the review, it will be converted into time coins and accumulated. Key information can be uploaded to the chain and deposited as a certificate.

> For implementation details such as record fields, audit standards, exception handling, etc., see the independent documents `02-ManualAudit.md` (manual audit) and `03-AutoAudit.md` (automatic audit).

## 10. Roles and Responsibilities

### 10.1 Students

- Proactively understand service requirements and time banking rules.
- Participate in volunteer service projects recognized by the school.
- Complete the service record form truthfully.
- Submit review materials on time.
- Pay attention to personal accumulated time and time coin balance.

### 10.2 Project leader or organizer supervisor

- Clarify service tasks and service requirements.
- Record the actual service status of students.
- Verify the service length and sign for confirmation.
- Provide necessary contact information and supporting documents to the school.

### 10.3 Teacher in Charge of the Grade

- Assist first-year students in understanding service requirements.
- Preliminary review of student submissions.
- Remind students who do not meet the standards to make up the time in time.
- Synchronize grade data with the Student Development Center.

### 10.4 Student Development Center

- Develop time banking rules and service recognition standards.
- Review volunteer service projects on and off campus.
- Manage student service records and time coin accounts.
- Handle special matters such as supplemental entries, reconsiderations, borrowing, and redemption.
- Regularly publish statistical reports and reminders.

### 10.5 Student Leader

- Assist in promoting the time bank system.
- Assist in collecting student questions and feedback.
- Support the organization and registration of volunteer service projects.
- Participate in student-side user experience optimization.

## 12. Audit mechanism

Audit is the core guarantee for the authenticity of time bank, and is divided into two types of implementations, each containing an independent risk control mechanism:

- **Manual audit (current stage)**: paper form + signature of the organizer + preliminary review by the teacher + review by the Student Development Center, see `02-ManualAudit.md` for details.
- **Automatic audit (POV witness audit)**: client-side desensitization + witness weak verification + AI risk control + multi-party mutual certification, see `03-AutoAudit.md` for details.
- **Evidence storage**: Key information from approved records may be hashed and stored on-chain as evidence (for evidence storage, not trading); see `04-Blockchain.md`.

## 13. Incentive system design

### 13.1 Non-material Benefits

Time banks should emphasize the sense of accomplishment of doing charity, so that students can achieve self-worth and inner satisfaction through service.

Mental stimulation can be enhanced in the following ways:

- Volunteer service growth records
- Annual Volunteer Service Report
- Public welfare story display
- Interviews with outstanding volunteers
- Campus charity list
- Demonstration of student-led public welfare projects

### 13.2 Actual income

Actual benefits should serve educational goals and should not weaken the public welfare attribute.

Can be designed as:

- Time coins can be exchanged for school cultural creations or souvenirs
- Priority in participating in public welfare project training
- Qualified to run for public welfare project leader
- Obtain recommendation or certification from the Student Development Center
- Inclusion in students’ comprehensive quality evaluation materials

### 13.3 Honor Level

| Level | Recommended accumulated time | Incentive methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bronze Volunteer | 25 hours | Electronic Badge or Stage Certification |
| Silver Volunteer | 75 hours | Volunteer Service Certificate |
| Gold Volunteer | 150 hours | Campus Display and Recognition |
| Outstanding Volunteer | 300 hours | Annual charity honors, key records of growth files |

Specific grade thresholds may be adjusted according to the school's annual policy.

### 13.4 Differentiated incentive principle (anti-utilitarianism)

Services from different sources should adopt differentiated ratios of time coins and spiritual incentives to weaken cheating and utilitarian motives from the source:

- **Spontaneous and sporadic public welfare** (such as picking up garbage, community mutual aid): give lower time coins (it is recommended to set a daily upper limit), but give higher spiritual incentives (medals, titles, class rankings) to protect the pure sense of honor for public welfare.
- **Designated bases may be able to preliminarily review projects**: Due to institutional endorsement or teacher preliminary review, the threshold for cheating is high, and medium and high time coins can be given.
- **High-investment projects** (such as reading reflections): There is a preliminary review and the time and mental cost is high, and higher time coins can be given.

The exchange value should be reasonably anchored to the time coin output to make cheating "unprofitable". For the audit implementation and risk control details of this principle, see `03-AutoAudit.md`.

## 14. Implementation and operation (manual stage)

Before the online system is launched, a transition model of "paper forms + electronic ledgers" will be adopted: signed by the organizer, initially reviewed by grade teachers, reviewed by the Student Development Center, and students are regularly reminded of progress. For the specific process, ledger specifications and form template, see `02-ManualAudit.md`.

## 15. Online systems and digitalization

Time Bank's online hosting platform is based on a complete Web system, providing student entrances and administrator/teacher entrances, and independently covering the entire process of project release, registration, recording, manual review, accounts, statistics and system management; in the third phase, a WeChat applet will be added that mainly serves POV on-site witnessing. For the specific design and implementation plan, see `05-OnlineSystem.md`; for automatic audit, see `03-AutoAudit.md`, and for blockchain evidence storage, see `04-Blockchain.md`.

## 16. Risks and Controls (Top Level)

The following table provides a system-level overview of risks. For detailed controls for manual review, automated review, and blockchain evidence storage, see `02-ManualAudit.md`, `03-AutoAudit.md`, and `04-Blockchain.md`, respectively.



| Risks | Performance | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| False services | Students submit services that did not actually occur | Require supervisor’s signature, contact information and supporting materials, and sample return visits |
| Exaggeration of duration | Actual service is less than declared duration | Establish reasonable duration standards and conduct secondary review of abnormal records |
| Project generalization | Non-public welfare activities are packaged as volunteer services | Clear identification standards, final review by the Student Development Center |
| Excessive utilitarianism | Students only focus on exchange benefits | Redemption focuses on honors and growth incentives, weakening material rewards |
| Review backlog | Large accumulation of forms causing delays | Set fixed review cycles and centralized review windows |
| Data loss | Paper materials are lost or spreadsheets are messed up | Paper filing numbers, electronic ledgers are backed up regularly |
| Loan abuse | Students rely on loan completion requirements | Set limit limits, approval conditions and return deadlines |

## 17. Implementation Plan

### 17.1 Phase 1: Policy Confirmation and Pilot Operation



Recommended cycle time: 1 month

- Clarify the service certification scope and duration rules.
- Confirm the service requirements for junior high school and high school.
- Unify paper forms and electronic ledger templates.
- Clarify the division of labor among the office, student development center, grade teachers and student leaders.
- Select a grade or several projects for a trial run.

### 17.2 Phase 2: Complete Web system construction and school-wide promotion

Recommended cycle: 1 to 2 semesters (see `05-OnlineSystem.md` for detailed plans and implementation plans)

- Merge the original "electronic ledger" and "online system construction" phases to build a one-time Web platform that can be put into formal operation.
- Build an independent **student portal**: project browsing and registration, service record submission, uploading of certification materials, review progress, time coin account, compliance progress, supplementary enrollment and review applications, and on-site notifications.
- Build a complete **administrator/teacher portal**: project and quota management, organizer management, manual review workbench, account and flow management, rule configuration, statistical dashboard, historical data import, data export, permissions, operation logs and exception handling.
- Support computer and mobile browsers with responsive Web. The second stage does not build or rely on WeChat applet, enterprise WeChat, DingTalk or other IM access.
- Complete the end-to-end acceptance from "project release - student registration - service records - material review - time coin entry - progress statistics - review/re-enrollment" to ensure that the entire process can be run based only on the Web.
- Import existing paper forms and electronic ledgers into the system, retaining the ability to manually review and archive paper materials.
- After a small-scale trial run, it will be promoted to the entire school, establish a monthly or semester statistical mechanism, and continue to collect feedback from students, teachers and organizers.

### 17.3 The third stage: WeChat applet and POV automatic review

Recommended period: 1 semester

- Add WeChat applet on top of the second-stage web platform and unified back-end, without duplicating the construction of projects, accounts and back-end management capabilities.
- The mini program is mainly oriented to POV on-site processes: location check-in, on-site shooting, witness scan code confirmation, terminal-side face desensitization, team member mutual certification and guardian endorsement.
- Access multi-modal AI preliminary review, image authenticity detection, statistical risk control and witness credit scoring; medium and low trust records are uniformly transferred to the Web management backend for second review.
- After the POV is approved, the service records of the Web system and the time coin account are reused to complete the accounting, ensuring that the Web and the mini program use the same data source, audit status and audit log.
- WeChat and other IM will not be used as pre-dependencies for the complete business closed loop in the second stage; when the mini program is unavailable, the basic business can still run normally through the Web.

### 17.4 Phase 4: Exchange and Expansion Mechanism Online

Periodic suggestions: after the online system is stable

- In the second phase, the web backend has already acquired relevant basic management capabilities. The focus of this phase is on rule confirmation, resource access and official activation.
- Determine the redemption items and redemption ratio.
- Pilot honor category and growth category redemption.
- Open lending and value-added functions with caution.
- Continuous optimization based on data evaluation.

## 19. Success Metrics

After the project is implemented, the effects can be evaluated through the following indicators:

- **Participation Rate**: The proportion of students who volunteer.
- **Compliance Rate**: The proportion of students who meet annual or graduation service requirements.
- **Review Efficiency**: The average time from submission of a service record to completion of its review.
- **Number of projects**: The number of volunteer service projects recognized by the school.
- **Total service hours**: The total number of volunteer service hours in the school.
- **Student Satisfaction**: Student feedback on service opportunities, documentation, and incentives.
- **Data Completeness Rate**: The proportion of service record fields that are complete and supporting materials are complete.
- **Public Welfare Impact**: Feedback from service recipients, communities or partner organizations.

## 20. Follow-up matters to be confirmed

In order to ensure the implementation of the plan, the school still needs to further confirm the following matters:

- Whether the cumulative requirements for students of different grades in junior high school are adjusted uniformly.
- Specific applicable grades and review points for the 300-hour high school graduation requirement.
- Whether to allow 0.5 hours as the minimum recording unit.
- Whether off-campus services must be reported in advance.
- Whether travel time can be included in the service time and the applicable conditions.
- Whether the loan function is online and the limit limit.
- Redeemable items, redemption ratio and approval method of the redemption function.
- Online system construction budget, cycle and technical person in charge.

## 22. Summary

The student volunteer service time bank is not only a tool to record service hours, but also a comprehensive mechanism to promote students’ public welfare participation, social responsibility cultivation and growth archive construction. Through the closed-loop design of "service time - time coin - time wealth - growth incentives", the school can further stimulate students' long-term motivation to participate in volunteer service while meeting graduation service requirements.

In the short term, it is recommended to use paper forms and electronic ledgers to complete the implementation of the system; in the medium term, build an online system to improve management efficiency; in the long term, gradually develop exchange, loan, value-added and data analysis functions to make time bank an important part of the student development system of the secondary school.
